analysis.investment_thesis: Network18 fails the Magic Formula on both dimensions — Earnings Yield is near-zero (~0.5% at EBIT of ₹44 Cr vs EV of ~₹8,900 Cr) and ROIC is equally negligible (~0.5%), making it uninvestable by any quantitative screen. A business that has generated positive operating cash flow in only 1 of the last 5 years, with cumulative FCF destruction of over ₹15,000 Cr since FY23, is not a business — it's a cash incinerator.
key_strengths: Reliance Industries parentage provides financial backstop and potential strategic synergies (JioCinema/Star India JV)
Strong brand portfolio: CNBC-TV18, MoneyControl, News18, Forbes India — meaningful consumer mindshare
Minimal EBITDA turning positive in FY26 (₹177 Cr) may signal post-restructuring stabilization
key_risks: Magic Formula metrics are near-zero: Earnings Yield ~0.5% (EBIT ₹44 Cr / EV ~₹8,900 Cr) — far below the 12% threshold
Free cash flow deeply negative in 4 of last 5 years: -₹8,869 Cr (FY24), -₹2,809 Cr (FY25), -₹77 Cr (FY26)
Finance costs growing at 11% CAGR while revenue contracts; borrowings rose to ₹3,288 Cr in FY26
red_flags: Operating CF positive in only 1/5 years — this is a fundamental business quality failure, not a temporary blip
Revenue collapsed from ₹9,297 Cr (FY24) to ₹2,121 Cr (FY26) — likely demerger of Viacom18/JioCinema, leaving a rump entity
Net loss of ₹1,777 Cr in FY25; net profit has been negative in 7 of last 10 years
EV/EBITDA of -98.59 and ROCE of just 3.02% — capital is being destroyed, not compounded
Massive balance sheet volatility (assets swung from ₹39,881 Cr in FY24 to ₹8,498 Cr in FY25) signals corporate complexity and opacity
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Applying the Magic Formula, Network18 is disqualifying on both axes. Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) comes in at roughly 0.5% — EBIT of ₹44 Cr in the most recent period against an Enterprise Value of ~₹8,900 Cr (Market Cap ₹5,616 Cr + Borrowings ₹3,288 Cr - minimal cash). The Magic Formula threshold is 12%+; this company is at 1/24th of that. Return on Capital is similarly broken at ~0.5% (₹44 Cr EBIT / ~₹8,200 Cr capital employed). A P/E of 153x on what appears to be a one-quarter blip of profitability, against a decade of mostly negative earnings, is not a "cheap" stock by any measure.

The structural picture is worse than the snapshot. The company appears to have shed its Viacom18/JioCinema assets into the Star India JV, leaving a rump media operation. Revenue has collapsed from ₹9,297 Cr (FY24) to ₹2,121 Cr (FY26). FCF has been negative for four consecutive years, destroying over ₹15,000 Cr in cumulative free cash. Finance costs are compounding at 11% annually. Even if the remaining business (news channels, MoneyControl, digital) stabilizes, the capital allocation history and corporate complexity under a Reliance holding structure make this deeply unattractive. The Magic Formula demands high returns on tangible capital at bargain prices — Network18 offers neither.
